original_value: Remote sensing (RS) image segmentation is an essential step in geographic object-based image analysis (GEOBIA) to ultimately derive “meaningful objects”. While many segmentation methods exist, most of them are not efficient for large data sets. Thus, the goal of this research is to develop an efficient parallel multi-scale segmentation method for RS imagery by combining graph theory and the fractal net evolution approach (FNEA). Specifically, a minimum spanning tree (MST) algorithm in graph theory is proposed to be combined with a minimum heterogeneity rule (MHR) algorithm that is used in FNEA. The MST algorithm is used for the initial segmentation while the MHR algorithm is used for object merging. An efficient implementation of the segmentation strategy is presented using data partition and the “reverse searching-forward processing” chain based on message passing interface (MPI) parallel technology. Segmentation results of the proposed method using images from multiple sensors (airborne, SPECIM AISA EAGLE II, WorldView-2, RADARSAT-2) and different selected landscapes (residential/industrial, residential/agriculture) covering four test sites indicated its efficiency in accuracy and speed. We conclude that the proposed method is applicable and efficient for the segmentation of a variety of RS imagery (airborne optical, satellite optical, SAR, high-spectral), while the accuracy is comparable with that of the FNEA method.

result.paraphrase: Remote sensing (RS) image segmentation is a key step in geographic object-based image analysis (GEOBIA) for deriving “meaningful objects.” Although numerous segmentation methods have been developed, most are inefficient on large datasets. This study therefore aims to create an efficient parallel multiscale segmentation approach for RS imagery by integrating graph theory with the fractal net evolution approach (FNEA). In particular, a minimum spanning tree (MST) algorithm from graph theory is combined with the minimum heterogeneity rule (MHR) algorithm used in FNEA: the MST handles the initial segmentation, and the MHR performs object merging. The proposed strategy is implemented efficiently through data partitioning and a “reverse searching-forward processing” chain built on message passing interface (MPI) parallel technology. Segmentation results from multiple sensors (airborne, SPECIM AISA EAGLE II, WorldView-2, RADARSAT-2) and different landscapes (residential/industrial, residential/agriculture) across four test sites show strong accuracy and speed efficiency. We conclude that the method is suitable and efficient for segmenting diverse RS imagery, including airborne optical, satellite optical, SAR, and hyperspectral data, with accuracy comparable to FNEA.
